item.title: When your AI agent sends the wrong email, it's already too late to scope the key (Sponsor)
item.description: 18% of teams had an AI agent send a wrong email last quarter, per Nylas's new survey. Nylas IAM gives each agent its own key, scoped to one mailbox if you want. Try to send on a read-only key and the Nylas gateway refuses it before Google or Microsoft ever sees the request. Every call gets logged, refusals included. Included on every plan.See how Nylas IAM works →

item.title: Now generally available: GKE dynamic slicing for higher resilience, and efficiency for TPUs (6 minute read)
item.description: Google Kubernetes Engine dynamic slicing is now generally available for TPUs. It separates slice formation from nodepool provisioning, cutting AI workload startup times by up to 5x and recovery times by 4.5x.

item.title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes: Hardware-enforced workload isolation on Amazon EKS (12 minute read)
item.description: AWS Nitro Sandboxes provides hardware-enforced workload isolation for Amazon EKS pods by running each one inside its own lightweight virtual machine. The feature allows users to enable strong security boundaries with a single line in the pod spec without changing container images or deployment pipelines. It offers isolated mode for standard protection and confidential mode for cryptographic attestation.

item.title: See what your Argo CD applications cost (10 minute read)
item.description: Cost Intelligence for Argo CD is an open-source extension that shows each application's cost in a UI tab, using the previous 24 hours of OpenCost data after each sync. It requires Argo CD 3.4 to 3.6 and OpenCost 1.121.1 or newer.

item.title: Kubernetes Gave AI Agents a Place to Run, But Not a Way to Recover (7 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes can restore an AI agent's environment but cannot record which steps finished, so restarted agents may repeat actions such as payments. The author argues for durable execution that logs each step, citing Dapr's workflow engine as an option.

item.title: 7 Production Habits We Learned at Wix. The Hard Way (10 minute read)
item.description: A Wix engineering lead details seven habits for reliable production systems, learned from eight years of operating the editor server team. The list includes using the Five Whys method to find root causes, running post-mortems without blame, and conducting team-wide on-call handovers. He emphasizes leaving the system better than you found it by fixing one small thing per shift.

item.title: Let your AI agents run code with strong isolation (Sponsor)
item.description: AI agents now write and execute code no human reviews first. AWS Nitro Sandboxes now runs each AI agent and container in its own lightweight VM on the AWS Nitro System, the same hardware isolation that separates every EC2 instance. Safely run untrusted, LLM-generated code with strong isolation and near bare-metal performance. Learn how it works here.

item.title: HA-MCP (GitHub Repo)
item.description: HA-MCP lets users configure and automate Home Assistant with AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT. The recommended integration installs directly through HACS or the built-in Marketplace on Home Assistant 2026.11+, runs in-process, and works across all installation types.

item.title: Astryx (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Astryx is an open-source design system with over 150 accessible components. It grew inside Meta over eight years to power more than 13,000 apps. The system is built on React 19 and StyleX, with a CLI designed for both human developers and AI assistants.

item.title: CloudNativePG becomes a CNCF Incubating Project (5 minute read)
item.description: CloudNativePG has moved from CNCF Sandbox to Incubation. The operator runs highly available PostgreSQL on Kubernetes and manages pods directly rather than through StatefulSets, handling failover, rolling updates, backups, and point-in-time recovery.

item.title: MCP Server Security Holes & How to Plug Them (18 minute read)
item.description: Model Context Protocol servers lack built-in authentication, rate limiting, and tool controls, creating security gaps for organizations. This guide explains how to deploy an AI Gateway to add token-based authentication and restrict which specific tools are available to users and agents.

item.title: Give developers a security tool they'll actually use (Sponsor)
item.description: Why choose between speed and security? 1Password secures developer secrets and AI-agent credentials at human and machine speed. Learn More.

item.title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents (3 minute read)
item.description: Entire, a Git forge led by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, is built for collaboration between developers and AI coding agents.

item.title: Authenticate external gRPC clients with Amazon VPC Lattice (14 minute read)
item.description: An Application Load Balancer validates external clients' JWTs, then an ECS proxy signs requests to private gRPC services with AWS SigV4.

item.title: Running Kubernetes at Its Extremes (5 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes documents limits of 5,000 nodes and 110 pods per node, and its default etcd storage limit is 2 GB.

item.title: Docker and ActiveState Extending Secure Defaults to the Packages Developers Install (5 minute read)
item.description: Docker partnered with ActiveState to extend its trusted content standard from base images to packages installed through pip, npm, and Maven. ActiveState rebuilds components from source and promises fixes within 5 business days for critical CVEs.

item.title: What's next for Octopus Feature Flags (6 minute read)
item.description: Octopus Feature Flags leave public preview for Octopus Cloud and arrive in self-hosted Octopus 2027.0, with rules-based targeting and phased automated rollouts. Existing flags require updated client SDKs before upgrading.

item.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85% (18 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare stopped rebuilding entire DNS zones for settings changes by identifying which records could be affected and grouping pending work for the same zone. Peak memory fell from 79 GiB to 12 GiB, and shorter waits between pipeline stages brought median build completion time down from 7.7 to 3.3 seconds.

item.title: Well, That Wasn't Fun: October 16 '26 (7 minute read)
item.description: Fly.io patched and rebooted its entire fleet over 10 hours in response to CVE-2026-99999, a Linux kernel bug that allowed guest VMs to read host memory. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to control two bytes of an IPv4 header, leading to firewall bypasses and out-of-bounds reads. Fly.io advises customers who sent unencrypted traffic between October 15 and 17 to rotate their credentials.

item.title: How to Import Existing Resources to OpenTofu [Tutorial] (15 minute read)
item.description: Spacelift compares the OpenTofu import CLI command with import blocks and recommends blocks because they appear in plan and apply. The tutorial covers for_each imports, the identity argument, and experimental config generation.

item.title: Production access shouldn't outlive the task (Sponsor)
item.description: A quick fix shouldn't require permanent admin access. With Teleport, engineers can request temporary access to servers, Kubernetes clusters, and databases. Approve requests through tools like Slack, then let privileges expire automatically.Learn More

item.title: Llama-modchip (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Llama-modchip runs the 284-billion-parameter DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a pure 64GB CPU with no GPU. It achieves up to 14.7 tokens per second using SwiGLU-H2 compression and cache optimizations. The tool also supports other models, including NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B at up to 111 tokens per second.

item.title: Claude-quickstarts (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Claude-quickstarts is a collection of projects designed to help developers build deployable applications using the Claude API. The repository includes examples for use cases like a customer support agent, a financial data analyst, and various computer use demos.

item.title: Compare AI agent changes with Online Experiments in Agent Observability (9 minute read)
item.description: Datadog Online Experiments compares AI agent variants on live traffic using evaluation scores alongside latency, cost, and error metrics. In an internal test, GPT-6 Luna cut estimated cost by 44.3 percent versus GPT-5.6 Luna with nearly identical quality scores.

item.title: Harness for Agents: Introducing a New Platform Experience (9 minute read)
item.description: Harness introduced a new platform experience built around a lightweight Go-based Delegate that runs every CD step in its own container. Worker Agents run as pipeline steps under existing approvals and audit logs, and the rollout is opt in through early access.

item.description: The kpt community released v1.0.0 after several years in pre-release.

item.title: Manage Kubernetes observability with DatadogInstrumentation (7 minute read)
item.description: Datadog introduced the DatadogInstrumentation custom resource, which holds a workload's checks, log collection, and APM settings in one Kubernetes resource.

item.title: What's new with Grafana variables: less clutter, easier reuse across dashboards, and more (7 minute read)
item.description: Grafana added section-level variables to rows and tabs generally available, letting users place controls near the panels they affect.

item.title: Alpine Linux Security Advisory: OpenSSH-server password authentication bypass (5 minute read)
item.description: A vulnerability in Alpine Linux's openssh-server package allows attackers to bypass password authentication and log in without knowing any password. The flaw affects releases 3.16 through 3.24 and allows remote access if the system has an account with no password set. Users should update openssh and restart sshd or disable password logins immediately.

item.title: Powering open infrastructure for autonomous agents (12 minute read)
item.description: Google donated Agent Substrate, gVisor, and OpenRL to the CNCF Sandbox and announced the general availability of Agent Substrate on GKE. Agent Substrate decouples stateful agent sessions from compute to restore idle sessions in under 500 milliseconds. The project achieves 10x standard container density and performs over 500 suspend and resume activations per second.

item.title: Running Production With Zero Stored Logs (6 minute read)
item.description: This post describes how to run a K3s platform of more than 15 microservices with no centralized log collection, relying on filtered Prometheus metrics and temporary verbose logging. It notes trade-offs, including the need to anticipate questions and unsuitability for audits requiring immutable trails.

item.title: When the Kubernetes API went silent: A three-layer networking mystery (8 minute read)
item.description: Google traced intermittent GKE API timeouts to three interacting failures: Private Service Connect reordered packets, Envoy kept half-closed sockets open, and a Linux TCP bug prevented those sockets from closing. Simultaneous packet captures at multiple points exposed the reordering, and a Linux kernel patch fixed the underlying TCP bug.

item.title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security (5 minute read)
item.description: Docker identifies five risks of autonomous AI agents, including prompt injection, credential exposure, and data exfiltration. It recommends isolation and governance through Docker Sandboxes and AI Governance rather than model improvements alone.

item.title: The Google SRE Book was written before AI started writing the code. (Sponsor)
item.description: Systems now change faster than teams can track, and AI features can look healthy while giving wrong answers. The AI SRE Handbook covers what that means for reliability, how to evaluate an AI SRE, and benchmark results from 25 real Sev1-3 incidents.Download the handbook.

item.title: agent-browser (GitHub Repo)
item.description: agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives AI agents a browser they can drive one shell command at a time. It reads pages as a compact accessibility tree and allows agents to interact with elements through refs. The tool supports Chrome for Testing, Mobile Safari, and various cloud browser providers.

item.title: Auto Ontology (GitHub Repo)
item.description: NVIDIA Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over enterprise data. The open source library builds context layers from metadata to enable deterministic query generation and more explainable AI for LLM workflows. It exposes this context to agents via MCP, CLI, and API access.

item.title: What Is the OpenTofu MCP Server and How to Use It (11 minute read)
item.description: Spacelift explains the official OpenTofu MCP server, which offers seven read-only tools for searching registry documentation for providers, modules, resources, and data sources. It runs from a hosted endpoint or locally with npx and never runs tofu commands or reads state.

item.title: Trace linkage: connect the dots between your app traces and database queries (4 minute read)
item.description: Grafana Cloud made trace linkage generally available in Database Observability. It connects OpenTelemetry application traces to database query data collected by Alloy, matching by query.

item.title: Reliability in the AI Era: AI That Works the Incident With You (6 minute read)
item.description: PagerDuty announced the PD Reliability Platform and PD Labs alongside its Paige SRE agent.

item.title: Evaluate your AI agents with Fireworks AI models in Datadog Agent Observability (3 minute read)
item.description: Datadog Agent Observability now supports Fireworks AI as a model provider.

item.title: Announcing the OpenTelemetry JavaScript SDK 3.0 (16 minute read)
item.description: OpenTelemetry JavaScript SDK 3.0 introduces ESM-only support and removes compatibility with older Node.js versions.

item.title: Bridging Alloy and OpenTelemetry: the OTel engine is now in Public Preview (8 minute read)
item.description: Grafana Alloy's OpenTelemetry engine is now in Public Preview as of Alloy v1.21.0. It runs standard OpenTelemetry Collector YAML configuration and supports Fleet Management for remote configuration. Users can run the OTel engine alongside the default engine or switch between them using an environment variable.

item.title: Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud (11 minute read)
item.description: Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud as a fully managed, serverless database. It includes autoscaling, scale to zero, instant branching, and point-in-time recovery to help teams build and ship faster without managing database infrastructure. Operational and analytical data share the same storage format.

item.title: Shopify Overexposed Scans GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run for Exposure (4 minute read)
item.description: Shopify Overexposed is an internal scanner that finds GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run services reachable without authentication. A rebuild on GCP Cloud Asset Inventory plus an anonymous HTTP probe cut inconclusive Ingress verdicts by about 80%.

item.title: The hidden latency inside your database (8 minute read)
item.description: PlanetScale Metal uses locally attached NVMe storage to eliminate network latency between compute and disk. This architecture avoids the IOPS limits of network-attached storage like EBS, where defaults are often capped at 3,000 IOPS. Benchmarks show an instance with local NVMe storage costs $551.15 per month compared to $1,513.82 for a comparable EBS setup.

item.title: Deep dive: Auto scaling response times on Amazon ECS (12 minute read)
item.description: Amazon ECS now offers high-resolution CPU and memory metrics published every 20 seconds for target tracking, allowing services to detect and respond to load changes faster than the default 60-second resolution. AWS benchmarks show time to trigger scale-out fell 76%, from 363 seconds to 86 seconds, and SLA breach time on Fargate decreased 69% in gradual ramp tests.

item.title: Floci (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Floci is a free, open-source local AWS emulator for development, testing, and CI that works without a cloud account or auth token. It supports standard tools like Terraform and the AWS CLI, and Lambda or RDS workloads run in real Docker containers for higher fidelity than mocks. The project also acts as a drop-in replacement for LocalStack.

item.title: Agent-Desktop (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Agent-Desktop is a CLI that enables AI agents to see and operate desktop applications on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree. It reads the accessibility tree as JSON, allowing agents to interact with elements without using screenshots or pixel matching.

item.title: Optimize your NRQL with Macros! (2 minute read)
item.description: New Relic introduced NRQL Macros, which save an expression as a reusable named shortcut called by prefixing the name with a dollar sign. Macros can simplify long WHERE clauses and update many dashboard widgets by changing one definition.

item.title: Detect when your AI agent copies a self-replicating prompt injection (11 minute read)
item.description: Datadog tested its AI Guard product against self-replicating prompt injections that OpenAI reported in September. AI Guard flagged a planted email as indirect prompt injection at 99.5% confidence and a planted CSV file as jailbreak and obfuscation.

item.description: Agentic AI risk comes from tool permissions that accumulate unnoticed, so boundaries belong in the platform.
